Kohaṃta
Pkt. poet. ref. in Svayambhūchhandas,
, p. 25 an. Jain Sāh. aur Itihās p. 385.

Kohala
poet. mentioned in Somadeva's Yaśastilakacampū (K.

, Vol. I. p. 459, verse 239).
See V. Raghavan, J. of the G. Jhā Res. Inst. I. iii. May 1944, p. 372.

Kohala
a. of Pkt. grammar. ref. to by Mārkaṇḍeya in his Pkt. gr. Probably like Bharata, Kohala dealt with Pkt. in his Nāṭya Śāstra.
See also Pischel, Comp. Gr. of the Pkt. Languages (Eng. transl. Benares, 1957), p. 35.

Kohala
ancient authority on Nāṭya Śāstra (dance, drama an. music); mentioned in Nāṭya Śāstra (GOS. edn.

.) a. one of the hundred sons of Bharata an. in the last ch. a. a. of Uttaratantra [Page099-a. dealing with whatever has been left unsaid by Bharata.
See NCC. II. p. 412b.
Q. by several later writers, Mataṅga (Bṛhaddeśī), Dāmodara (Kuṭṭanīmata), Rājaśekhara, Abhinavagupta, Śāradātanaya an. several other still later writers on music an. dance.
From Abhinavagupta's C. on Nāṭya Śāstra it appears that he was the first to define the Uparūpakas. From a q. in Sarvānanda's C. Ṭīkāsarvasva on Amara (TSS. edn. I. p. 119), Kohala is seen to have dealt with Kathā an. Ākhyāyikā also.
Several later texts, noted below, are associated with him singly or with other sages, Dattila, Mataṅga an. Śārdūla. Perhaps his original work is lost, but he is remembered a. the most important ancient writer after Bharata.
See V. Raghavan, J. of the Music Academy, Madras. III. p. 17; Sangeet Natak Akadami Bulletin 5, 1956, p.. 20-1, 23-4; Bhoja's Śṛṅgāra Prakāśa (1963), p.. 535-7, 540-1, 544-6, 550, 562, 567, 569, 576 fn., 577-9, 589, 615; also his ‘Uparūpakas an. Nṛtyaprabandhas’, Sangeet Natak 2 an. Samskrita Ranga Annual V. p.. 33-4; an. ‘Music in ancient Indian drama’, Art an. Letters, the J. of the Royal India, Pakistan, Ceylon Society, London XXVIII. i. 1954, p.. 10-18; J. of the Music Academy, Madras,

, p. 90; Sangeet Natak Akadami Bulletin 4, 1956, p.. 5, 6, 11, 12.
See also Proceed. AIOC. Patna, 1930, p.. 777-80, P. V. Kane, ‘Fragments from Kohala’.
--Abhinayaśāstra.

(with Telugu meaning). [Page099-b]
--Uttaratantra; a supplement to Bharata's Nāṭya Śāstra mentioned a. Kohala's work towards the end of Nāṭya Śāstra (ch. XXXV. śl. 65, Kasi edn.) itself.
--Kohalamata. See below.
--Kohalarahasya. See below.
--Tālalakṣaṇa.

/1.
--Saṅgītameru on music an. dance. Kohala-Śārdūlasaṁvāda in Anuṣṭubh verses. Q. extensively on Karavartanās by Kallinātha on Saṅgītaratnākara, ch. 7.
From the q.s here this appears to be a late work but ascribed to Kohala.

Kohala(kuṣmāṇḍakavi)
ref. to in Mahāpurāṇa.
See Jain Sāh. aur Itihās p. 325 fn. 1.

Kohalamata
music; in the form of a dialogue between Kohala an. Mataṅga.

Kohalarahasya
music. in the form of a dialogue between Kohala an. Mataṅga on Rāgas appropriate in certain contexts.

Kohalīputrāḥ
a Vedic school mentioned in Taitt.

.
See Bhagavad Datta, Vaidik Vāṅmaya kā Itihās I. p. 234.
